clue.text: Possibly recruit officer to company

indicators.note: to here means added on to, so the officer is placed after the company

parts.note: LT is short for lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: A sergeant wonders whether to attach a new recruit's officer to a particular company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' warns that a colt is only one kind of recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a colt is a young, inexperienced player, a novice newly taken on, like a recruit.

clue.text: Person involved in vocal parts of Tosca is producing this

definitions.text: Person involved in vocal parts of Tosca is producing this

indicators.note: involved in means one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: the vowels of Tosca, its voiced letters, are O and A
PER as in 'per person', a Latin word for each person

explanation.surface: Someone singing Tosca's vocal parts is putting on this kind of show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocal parts' sounds like singing roles but means the vowels of the word Tosca; the whole clue also defines, since Tosca is Puccini's famous work for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is a Puccini work for singers and orchestra, so performing its vocal parts means staging one of these.

clue.text: This time I left yard clutching last of timber with some eagerness

indicators.note: clutching means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of timber

explanation.surface: A woodworker leaves the timber yard, keen and in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of timber, R, sits inside the run THISTILY, just after THI.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something thirstily is doing it greedily and keenly, like a parched drinker, hence eagerly.

clue.text: Trainee keen to retain misplaced trust? Not right

indicators.note: to retain means the keen word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: keen means ardent

indicators.note: misplaced signals the letters of trust are put out of order
not right says the letter standing for right is dropped

explanation.surface: A young enthusiast wonders whether trust in them has been misplaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'trust' is used loosely; 'Not right' drops R from it, and 'misplaced' scrambles the remaining TUST into TSTU.
explanation.definitionFit: An art student is learning a craft at college, a trainee in painting or design.

clue.text: Line encapsulating source of Scott's reputation?

definitions.text: Line encapsulating source of Scott's reputation?

parts.words: Line encapsulating source of Scott's reputation?
parts.note: Captain Scott won lasting fame on his South Pole expedition; the line of latitude enclosing that polar region is meant

explanation.surface: A biographer looks for the single line that sums up the root of Scott's fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott here is Robert Falcon Scott, the British explorer who died returning from the South Pole in 1912. 'Line' sounds like a line of text but is a line of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a line of latitude round the southern polar region, the frozen continent where Scott made his name.

clue.text: Excessively delay adopting black kit

parts.note: excessively means too

indicators.note: adopting means taking the next piece in

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind or delay
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles far too long before taking up a black outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A container of tools for a job is a workman's kit, the gear carried to the site.

clue.text: Novel astonishes and lures possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A new thing amazes people and tempts them, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as an adjective meaning new, but it is a noun: Hemingway's 1926 book.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway's first major book, about expatriates in Paris and Pamplona, is a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Scientist picked up circuit board feeding in current

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means the letters are lifted so they read bottom to top
feeding in means going inside the other piece

parts.note: a circuit board in a computer is called a card
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An electrician lifts a circuit board with power running into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns CARID, the I inside CARD, upside down in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac was the British physicist who predicted antimatter and shared the 1933 Nobel prize.

clue.text: Fruit I found in entrance, squashed

indicators.note: squashed means crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds a piece of fruit crushed in the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a stone fruit sold in summer.

clue.text: Slave with line lassoing one flowering plant

indicators.note: lassoing means roping something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a helot was a serf in ancient Sparta
I is the Roman numeral one
a rope is a line

explanation.surface: A slave with a rope ropes in a single animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden plant with fragrant purple blooms is named for turning towards the sun.

clue.text: Frontless dress to cause a stir?

indicators.note: frontless means losing its first letter

parts.note: a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: Wearing a dress with no front would be bound to scandalise people.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to shake or unsettle, as in rocking the boat, which stirs things up.

clue.text: Drunken barflies dislocated bone

indicators.note: drunken means staggering about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Drunk pub regulars have dislocated a bone in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dislocated' looks like a second anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition: these lower ribs are not joined directly to the breastbone, so they are humorously out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower ribs that do not attach straight to the sternum are a kind of bone of the chest.

clue.text: Man with balls getting reduced notice being naked

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: uncle is slang for a pawnbroker, whose sign is three golden balls
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A man with a ball is cut down by a short note telling him he is undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker; the pawnshop sign is three hanging golden balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclad is being undressed, without clothes on, so it means the same as nude.

clue.text: Lines, namely comment on passing time

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely
RIP, rest in peace, is said of someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone writes a few lines remarking on how time goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' means a death, not time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's lines are written in the play's text, the words they speak on stage.

clue.text: Excited, ready to fire a round

parts.note: to cock a gun is to make it ready to shoot
a hoop is round, a ring

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled is ready to let off a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be extremely pleased and jubilant, crowing like a cockerel, is to be elated.

clue.text: Acknowledge a lot of rocks, including one of the heaviest rocks

indicators.note: including means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: to grant is to concede or acknowledge
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink on the rocks

explanation.surface: A geologist admits that many of the specimens include some of the densest stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' first means ice in a drink, then the stony sort in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for things made of granite, a hard, dense igneous stone.

clue.text: Lover keen on engaging a second artist

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
a mo is a moment, a second
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A lover is keen on hiring a second painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian word for a male sweetheart or admirer, a beloved.

clue.text: Arctic vessel circling island in the Channel Isles

indicators.note: circling means going round and coming back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards
in means the island sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a cay is a small low island or reef
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A polar ship sails round one of the islands off the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' is the reversal signal, not a container: CAY inside THECI gives THCAYECI, which 'circling' turns back. The Channel Isles are British Crown dependencies near Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: This craft has runners and a sail for skimming across frozen surfaces, fitting for polar waters.

clue.text: Experiments with bells around railway

indicators.note: around means the bells go round the other piece

parts.note: tings are bell-like ringing sounds

explanation.surface: Someone tests bells set up round a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Tryings are attempts or trials, the things done to test whether something works.

clue.text: Roof-worker succeeded afterwards

parts.note: S is the genealogy abbreviation for succeeded
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: The roofer turned up and got on with the job later on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who covers roofs with flat stone tiles is a roofer.

clue.text: Witch getting lot of profit as prophet

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

indicators.note: lot of means most of, so the last letter goes

parts.note: gain is profit

explanation.surface: A witch makes a fortune by setting herself up as a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profit' and 'prophet' sound alike but this is not a sound clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggai is a minor Old Testament seer, author of a short biblical book.

clue.text: Catch involved about welcome

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside the other piece

parts.note: to get is to catch
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A fisherman's catch is the cause of a warm reception.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone is to receive them with words of hello, a welcome.

clue.text: Juvenile holding power in resort

indicators.note: holding means keeping the next piece inside

parts.note: a youth is a juvenile
arm means power, as in the strong arm of the law

explanation.surface: A young offender has power over a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Yarmouth is a seaside holiday town in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Yarmouth, often shortened, is an English seaside holiday town on the Norfolk coast.

clue.text: Transactions almost complete for ownerless items

parts.note: TR abbreviates transactions, as in the learned journals of societies

indicators.note: almost means one letter short at the end

parts.note: over means complete, finished

explanation.surface: Deals nearly done for some unclaimed property.
explanation.walkthrough: In English law, treasure trove is valuables found hidden with no traceable owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove, as in treasure trove, is a found store of valuables whose owner is unknown.

clue.text: Wine writing with no little power

indicators.note: with no means the following piece is taken away

parts.note: prose is writing
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A wine writer turns out words that lack force.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosé is a pink wine, made with brief skin contact from red grapes.

clue.text: Is officer chasing quantity of film stars?

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the officer follows the rest

parts.note: film is stored in a can
taken as written
a major is an army officer

explanation.surface: An officer asks if he is chasing a reel of film featuring celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests film stars but means celestial ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dog is a constellation, a group of celestial bodies that includes Sirius.

clue.text: A lot of money is surrounding man with operating system: the culminating point

indicators.note: surrounding means going around the other pieces

parts.note: a pot is a large sum of money
taken as written
he stands for a man
OS is the computing abbreviation for operating system

explanation.surface: A fortune is spent on a man with a computer system, the high point of his career.
explanation.definitionFit: An apotheosis is the peak or highest development of something, its climax.

clue.text: Old variables, involving core of algebra, call for attention

indicators.note: involving means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: y and z are standard variables in algebra

indicators.note: core of picks the central letter

explanation.surface: An old maths problem with variables cries out for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a town crier or court official, demanding silence and listening.
